readmeHtml:
astrid-capsule-memory

Cross-session memory for Astrid OS agents.

In the OS model, this capsule is the persistent swap file. It carries context across session boundaries so the agent remembers what happened last time.

How it works

Hooks into prompt_builder.v1.hook.before_build. On each prompt assembly cycle:

  1. Reads .astrid/memory.md from the workspace via the VFS
  2. Wraps the content in a # Memory section
  3. Publishes an appendSystemContext hook response on the per-request response topic

If the file is missing or empty, the capsule is a no-op.

Size cap

Agent-written content can grow without limit (unlike human-authored AGENTS.md), so a 32KB hard cap prevents unbounded context window consumption. Content beyond the limit is truncated at a UTF-8 character boundary with a [Memory truncated] marker.

Read-only

This capsule handles the read/inject side only. The agent writes to .astrid/memory.md using existing filesystem tools (write_file, replace_in_file) from astrid-capsule-fs. No new tools needed.

Development

cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release

readmeExcerpt:
# astrid-capsule-memory




**Cross-session memory for [Astrid OS](https://github.com/unicity-astrid/astrid) agents.**

In the OS model, this capsule is the persistent swap file. It carries context across session boundaries so the agent remembers what happened last time.

## How it works

Hooks into `prompt_builder.v1.hook.before_build`. On each prompt assembly cycle:

1. Reads `.astrid/memory.md` from the workspace via the VFS
2. Wraps the content in a `# Memory` section
3. Publishes an `appendSystemContext` hook response on the per-request response topic

If the file is missing or empty, the capsule is a no-op.

## Size cap

Agent-written content can grow without limit (unlike human-authored `AGENTS.md`), so a 32KB hard cap prevents unbounded context window consumption. Content beyond the limit is truncated at a UTF-8 character boundary with a `[Memory truncated]` marker.

## Read-only

This capsule handles the read/inject side only. The agent writes to `.astrid/memory.md` using existing filesystem tools (`write_file`, `replace_in_file`) from `astrid-capsule-fs`. No new tools needed.

## Development

```bash
cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release
```

## License

Dual-licensed under [MIT](LICENSE-MIT) and [Apache 2.0](LICENSE-APACHE).

Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Joshua J. Bouw and Unicity Labs.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A cross-session persistent swap file capsule providing memory for Astrid OS agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository implements the `astrid-capsule-memory` capsule, which serves as a persistent cross-session swap file for agents running on Astrid OS. It hooks directly into the prompt assembly cycle to read a memory file from the workspace via the Virtual File System (VFS). By automatically wrapping this content in a dedicated section and appending it to the system context, it ensures the agent remembers what happened in previous sessions. This seamless context preservation allows agents to maintain long-term memory across distinct operational boundaries without manual state management.
keyFeatures: Cross-session persistence: Carries context across session boundaries so the agent remembers past events.
Automated prompt injection: Hooks into the before-build cycle to automatically append memory to the system context.
VFS integration: Reads and interacts with a dedicated memory file directly from the workspace filesystem.
Graceful degradation: Functions as a safe no-op if the memory file is missing or empty.
Astrid OS compatibility: Designed specifically as a core operational capsule within the Astrid OS environment.

useCases.title: Maintaining agent context
useCases.description: Users deploy the capsule so their Astrid OS agent remembers instructions and state from a previous day's work session.

useCases.title: Long-term task execution
useCases.description: Complex, multi-step agent tasks rely on the memory capsule to store progress and resume correctly after an interruption.

useCases.title: Automated state recovery
useCases.description: Developers use the capsule's hook system to automatically load saved workspace context into the agent's prompt without manual intervention.

useCases.title: Iterative prompt building
useCases.description: The system aggregates memory safely over time, allowing the agent to continuously learn from its interactions within the workspace.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers and operators building and running AI agents on Astrid OS who need reliable, cross-session memory management.
